definition.description: REV | Ops | Failure Alert. Child flow called from the run-after failed/timed-out path of every other flow in this solution. Writes exactly one rev_errorlog row and alerts the process owner, so no failure is silent (FR-010, NFR-016). HOLDS NO PERSONAL DATA: the caller passes a record REFERENCE, never a name, contact detail or narrative fragment (NFR-012, C-DOM-004). The structural control is the rev_errorlog schema itself, which has no column capable of holding personal data (TAD NFR-012 rationale); the truncation below is defence in depth, not the control. Compliance caveat recorded in TAD section 5.14: a reference that resolves to a living person is strictly pseudonymised personal data rather than anonymous, which is why this table carries a 90-day operational retention and no trustee access (risk A-R12, flagged for DPO confirmation).

metadata.description: Environment variable. The alert recipient, injected per environment at import (C-TECH-047). Never a literal address.
Environment variable. Outlook fallback recipient used when this flow's own Dataverse or Teams step fails - so a failure of the failure handler is still visible (TAD section 4 fallback).

manual.description: Child-flow trigger. Called only by other flows in this solution, never by a person. Every input is a value the caller already holds - no input requires the caller to read a record.

text.title: Flow name
text.description: The display name of the calling flow, for example REV | Intake | WordPress to Dataverse.

text_1.title: Run id
text_1.description: The calling flow's run identifier, so the native Power Automate run history can be reached from the log row.

text_2.title: Error message
text_2.description: The platform error text. MUST NOT contain personal data. Callers pass the error only, never the payload that caused it.

text_3.title: Record reference
text_3.description: A reference such as REV-2026-014 or the source submission id. A REFERENCE ONLY - never a name, email address or narrative.

text_4.title: Severity
text_4.description: Information, Warning, Error or Critical. Mapped to the rev_errorseverity option value below.

Map_severity_to_option_value.description: Maps the caller's severity word to the rev_errorseverity option value: 1 Information, 2 Warning, 3 Error, 4 Critical. Anything unrecognised becomes 3 (Error) rather than being dropped - an unclassifiable failure is still a failure.

Truncate_error_message.description: Caps the message at 2000 characters. Defence in depth only (NFR-012): the real control is that rev_errorlog has no column able to hold personal data. A platform error can be very long and an unbounded write would be the one place a payload fragment could reach the log.
Truncate_error_message.inputs: @if(greater(length(coalesce(triggerBody()?['text_2'], '')), 2000), concat(substring(coalesce(triggerBody()?['text_2'], ''), 0, 2000), ' [truncated]'), coalesce(triggerBody()?['text_2'], 'No error message supplied by the calling flow.'))

Write_error_log_row.description: One row per failure. rev_name is an autonumber (ERR-yyyyMMdd-nnnn) so it is not set here. rev_resolved is written false explicitly so the row appears in the Unresolved Errors view immediately - the view the PRD smoke test asserts is empty (FR-010).

Alert_process_owner_in_Teams.description: 1:1 chat to the process owner, never a channel post (ADR-015). Carries the flow name, the run id, the record reference and the error text - all four of which are non-personal by the caller's contract. No applicant name and no narrative.

parameters.body/messageBody:
Grant automation failure

Flow: @{triggerBody()?['text']}
Severity: @{triggerBody()?['text_4']}
Record reference: @{triggerBody()?['text_3']}
Error log row: @{outputs('Write_error_log_row')?['body/rev_name']}
Run id: @{triggerBody()?['text_1']}

@{outputs('Truncate_error_message')}

Open the Error Log in REV Grant Administration to mark this resolved.

Fallback_email_when_logging_or_alerting_.description: A failure of the failure handler must not be silent. If the Dataverse write or the Teams post fails, send to the service mailbox instead (TAD section 4 documented fallback). Deliberately carries no record reference: at this point the flow cannot be sure the reference was safely bounded, and the recipient can reach the run from the run id.

parameters.emailMessage/Subject: Grant automation: failure alert could not be logged
parameters.emailMessage/Body:
REV | Ops | Failure Alert could not write to the Error Log table or could not post to Teams.

Calling flow: @{triggerBody()?['text']}
Calling run id: @{triggerBody()?['text_1']}
Severity reported: @{triggerBody()?['text_4']}

Investigate in the Power Automate run history. The original failure is NOT recorded in Dataverse.

Respond_to_calling_flow.description: A child flow must end in a Response or the parent hangs until timeout. This responds 200 whatever happened, on purpose: the parent has ALREADY failed, and a failing error handler must not turn one failure into two. The response body tells the parent whether the row was written so a reviewer reading the parent's run history can tell the difference.
